# Launcher

Plugin ID `launcher`. Links to your infrastructure.

The launcher is a list of links to your infrastructure, shown as the Infrastructure section of the
Apps page. The links come from a YAML or JSON file
(`plugins.launcher.file`, see [`docs/launcher.example.yaml`](../launcher.example.yaml)) or are
listed inline (`plugins.launcher.links`).

## What it shows

### Pages

No page of its own.

### Panels on other pages

| Page | Panel | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Apps (`apps.sources`) | Infrastructure links | `infrastructure` |

### Topics

Published on `/api/v1/stream` and `/api/v1/topics/{topic}`:

| Topic | Payload | What |
|---|---|---|
| `launcher.links` | `LauncherData` | The launcher's infrastructure links. |

## Settings

Every setting is under `plugins.launcher` in the config file and is also in the [configuration reference](../configuration.md#pluginslauncher), with the rules for all of them: the layers, the `_FILE` form of each variable and secret references. _Restart_ marks a setting that applies only when dash restarts; a change to any other restarts the plugin in place.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Secret | Restart | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.launcher.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_LAUNCHER_TYPE` | string | - | no | no | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.launcher.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_LAUNCHER_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.launcher.file` | `DASH_PLUGINS_LAUNCHER_FILE` | string | - | no | no | Path of a YAML or JSON file with the launcher's links (see docs/launcher.example.yaml). The file is read when the launcher starts: restart dash, or change the launcher's settings, to read it again; an unreadable file makes the launcher report an error. Not together with links. |
| `plugins.launcher.links` | `DASH_PLUGINS_LAUNCHER_LINKS` | list of objects (JSON) | - | no | no | The launcher's links, inline: a list of {name, href, icon, description}. icon is an icon name (resolved against ui.iconBaseURL; without it the link shows a letter tile), a same-origin path, or an image URL under ui.iconBaseURL. Not together with file. |

- Mount a file from a ConfigMap and point `plugins.launcher.file` at it, or list the links in
  `plugins.launcher.links`.
- An unreadable file makes the launcher plugin report `error`, and dash still starts.
- An invalid link in `plugins.launcher.links` is refused when the configuration loads, and so is
  an inline `icon` outside the three forms (another origin than `ui.iconBaseURL`, `javascript:`,
  `data:`), named by its entry. Such an icon in the launcher file makes the launcher report
  `error` with a warning that names the entry, and dash still starts.
- A link's `href` that is not `http:` or `https:` is shown as text, not a link.

## Actions

None: the plugin only reads.

## Demo twin

With `DASH_DEMO=true` dash runs the plugin's demo twin instead: the same manifest, enabled and configured whatever the settings say, publishing made-up data from the fake lab in `internal/demo/world` and contacting nothing.
